question: Can integrated reference uncertainty and further-record prediction diagnose confident wrong maps?
outcome: The 2,592-trial grid spans 24 new systems and 216 conditions. Integrated reference uncertainty removes confident wrong cases in the unchanged administrative conditions but leaves failures after a process change. Erroneous supplied identities usually worsen held-out score, with saved exceptions under the constrained model.
challenge: Finite reference parameters, a mismatched stationary model and a wrong supplied identity contribute different failures. Archived source-path imports initially sought the helper under the wrong directory.
remedy: Dirichlet-integrated ordered-sequence scores, exact mapping enumeration, paired held-out populations, separate identity conditions, frozen-byte execution with original path context and independent scalar/sequential scores for all 216 conditions.
retry_when: A new observation-selection, variable-inventory, segmentation or physically grounded identity model changes the supplied benchmark assumptions.
